study: Short squeeze (forced buyers): when a heavily shorted liquid stock breaks out on volume, do the shorts' forced buy-backs make it keep outperforming over the next week - more than the same kind of breakout in a normally shorted stock?
registered_at: 2026-10-23, before any FINRA file is downloaded and before any outcome
origin: Operator 10/23 ('sell me this pen'): buy where there is a reason for the NEXT buyer to arrive, not where the name merely looks right. Of the forced-buyer ideas, month-end is the only strong result (+20.6 bp), the closing auction is blocked (Databento 402), index changes are priced at the announcement, and post-earnings drift was tested 10/7 (2023-26 -24 / -44 bp). Short covering is the one untested forced-buyer flow.
prior: LOW (~5-10%). The literature's main short-interest finding is the opposite: heavily shorted stocks UNDERPERFORM on average (shorts are informed). Squeezes are rare tail events. In favour: conditioning on a breakout (shorts already under pressure) is where forced covering concentrates, and the comparison against normally shorted breakouts isolates it.

data.short_interest: FINRA public files https://cdn.finra.org/equity/otcmarket/biweekly/shrt{YYYYMMDD}.csv, every settlement date 2020-01-15 .. 2026-09-30 (~161 files, ~350 MB; amended (11)): currentShortPositionQuantity, averageDailyVolumeQuantity, daysToCoverQuantity (DTC), marketClassCode, symbolCode, settlementDate. Stored on the mini under data/finra_short_interest/ (git-ignored).
data.availability: NO LOOK-AHEAD: a report counts only from its PUBLICATION, taken as the settlement date + 9 trading days (FINRA publishes about 7 business days after settlement; 9 is conservative). Information: + 12 trading days.
data.prices: Alpaca daily bars (data-only account, adjustment=all for returns, raw for the price floor), SPY for beta and market returns.

universe: Common stocks listed on NYSE / Nasdaq / NYSE American (marketClassCode in NYSE, NNM / NSC / NASDAQ codes as found, AMEX); ETFs and funds excluded (Alpaca asset name containing ETF / Fund / Trust / iShares / SPDR / ProShares / Direxion, or FINRA issueName likewise; the rule is applied identically to both groups). Each event day: raw prior close >= $20 and 20-day mean dollar volume >= $20M (the desk's floor and liquidity rule).
feature: DTC from the latest PUBLISHED report before the trigger day. HIGH = DTC in the top decile of that report's eligible universe; NORMAL = DTC below the 70th percentile of that report. The 70-90th percentile band is excluded (a gap between groups).
trigger: A BREAKOUT day: close / previous close - 1 >= +3% AND volume >= 2 x the 20-day median volume AND the close >= the prior 20-day high close. First trigger per name per report window (dedup: one event per name per publication window); the trigger day must be at least 1 trading day after publication.
trade: Buy at the trigger day's close (an MOC order), sell at the close 5 trading days later (PRIMARY). 1, 10 and 20 days are information.
returns: Beta-adjusted: name return - beta x SPY return over the same hold, beta from the 60 trading days before the trigger (OLS, daily); minus 10 bp round-trip cost (30 bp also printed).
statistic: PRIMARY = mean of HIGH-DTC breakout events minus mean of NORMAL-DTC breakout events, with week-clustered SE (events clustered by the trigger's calendar week) and, separately, a calendar-time version (daily portfolio of open positions, Newey-West 5 lags); the SMALLER t is used.
power: Outcome-blind count step before any return is computed: HIGH and NORMAL event counts per half, and the projected MDE from the dispersion of 5-day beta-adjusted returns of ALL eligible names on random dates (no event outcome). If the MDE > 50 bp in a half, or HIGH < 150 events in a half: UNDERPOWERED, not scored.
pass: In BOTH halves: PRIMARY >= +50 bp net (10 bp cost) with t >= 2.0; HIGH events' own beta-adjusted mean > 0 at 30 bp cost; PRIMARY stays > 0 after dropping the top 3 weeks and (separately) the top 5 names; the HIGH-minus-NORMAL sign holds at the +12-day availability lag. FAIL: t <= -2 in a half, or the 97.5% upper bound < +50 bp in both halves. Otherwise UNDERPOWERED. A PASS earns a held-out check on 2017-2019 FINRA files and a forward paper prereg; never a desk change by itself.
control_logic: NORMAL-DTC breakouts carry the same breakout momentum, liquidity screen and calendar, so HIGH minus NORMAL isolates the short-covering fuel; the same-week clustering absorbs market regime.
information_only: HIGH-DTC names WITHOUT a trigger (the documented short-interest anomaly; expected negative) - same hold, random eligible days
DTC deciles of breakout events (a dose-response curve)
short interest change (changePercent) up vs down into the trigger
the 2020-2021 meme-squeeze era vs the rest
no_retuning: the 3% / 2x volume / 20-day-high breakout, top decile vs < 70th percentile, the 9-day publication lag, 5-day hold, $20 / $20M screen, halves and the 50 bp bar are fixed.
declared_deviations: a multi-day hold (MOC in, MOC out), not the desk's 3-minute scalps; it is a separate book if it ever passes
DTC uses FINRA's own ADV; float-based short interest % is not available free historically
symbol changes and delistings: events whose name has no bars over the hold are dropped and counted (survivorship declared)
ETF exclusion by name keywords is approximate and applied to both groups
script: tools/studies/short_squeeze.py (to be written): --fetch (FINRA files, after operator approval), --bars, count step, --score after a result-skeptic READY.

amended.when: 2026-10-23, before any download or outcome, after result-skeptic FIX FIRST (11 items).
changes: (1) ENTRY: the breakout is known only at D0's close, so the PRIMARY entry is the D+1 CLOSE (MOC the next day) and the 5-day hold runs from there; buying at the D0 close is information only (not tradeable as defined).

(2) PUBLICATION: a report counts from settlement + 10 trading days (FINRA publishes ~7 business days after settlement; 10 covers holidays). Information: + 12. CDN files may carry later revisions; rows with revisionFlag or stockSplitFlag set are dropped and counted per group.

(3) COVERAGE STEP before any event or return: per file, row counts by marketClassCode; the code list is frozen from it; if the count of eligible NYSE / Nasdaq / NYSE American common stocks changes by more than 25% between the half means, the halves are declared not comparable and reported separately (no pooled read).

(4) POINT-IN-TIME: the $20 / $20M screen and the DTC deciles use data ending at the PUBLICATION date (20 sessions of dollar volume ending there), frozen per report. Trigger inputs (20-day median volume, 20-day high close) and the 60-day beta end at D0 - 1 (the trigger day's own close and volume are the breakout). Bars are split-adjusted (adjustment = all) so reverse splits cannot fake a breakout; the price floor uses the raw close.

(5) MATCHED CONTROL (PRIMARY): each HIGH breakout is compared with NORMAL breakouts in the same calendar week AND the same tercile of 60-day volatility AND the same tercile of 20-day dollar volume (terciles of all eligible breakout events in H1, applied to both halves); the PRIMARY is the mean over HIGH events of (HIGH return - mean of its matched NORMAL returns); unmatched HIGH events are counted. The unmatched comparison and a difference-in-differences ((HIGH breakout - HIGH random day) - (NORMAL breakout - NORMAL random day)) are information.

(6) DTC: FINRA's daysToCoverQuantity is PRIMARY; our own short position / 20-day SIP ADV ending at settlement is computed, its Spearman correlation with FINRA's field and the HIGH cutoff per report are printed before scoring.
(7) COST is charged to the HIGH trade only (10 bp; 30 bp printed); the matched NORMAL control is gross.

(8) POWER: MDE = 2.84 x max(SE week-clustered, SE name-clustered, SE calendar-time) of the actual PRIMARY series, printed before any mean is read; MDE > 50 bp in a half -> UNDERPOWERED, not scored. Floor: >= 150 matched HIGH events per half.

(9) VERDICT: powered and not PASS = FAIL (no powered UNDERPOWERED). t = the smallest of week-clustered, name-clustered and calendar-time NW(5). No new event for a name while its previous event's hold is open.

(10) SURVIVORSHIP: bars fetched per event with the symbol as of the event date; a name delisted or halted mid-hold exits at its last available close (not dropped); drops for missing bars are counted per group; the run aborts if drops exceed 2% of events or differ between groups by more than 1 point. The 'Trust' keyword also removes REITs (declared, both groups).

(11) MULTIPLICITY: no information cell can be promoted without its own prereg. The settlement window ends at the last file PUBLISHED at least 1 day before the run (2026-09-30 settlement, published ~2026-10-09): 2020-01-15 .. 2026-09-30, ~161 files. The 2017-2019 held-out check gets the same coverage step.
